text: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam fell ill.

Jeroboam said to his wife, "Get up, disguise yourself so no one will recognize you as Jeroboam's wife, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there—the one who told me I would be king over this people.
Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."
So Jeroboam's wife did as he said. She went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see; his eyes had failed because of his age.
But the LORD had said to Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill. Say such and such to her. When she arrives, she will be pretending to be someone else."
So when Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why pretend to be someone else? I have been sent to you with heavy news.
Go, tell Jeroboam: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel.

I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you, but you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing only what was right in my eyes.
You have done more evil than all who came before you. You went and made yourself other gods and cast images, provoking me to anger, and you have thrust me behind your back.

Therefore I am bringing disaster on the house of Jeroboam. I will cut off from Jeroboam every last male in Israel, slave or free. I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as a man burns dung, until it is gone.
Those of Jeroboam's house who die in the city the dogs will eat, and those who die in the open country the birds of the sky will eat—for the LORD has spoken.
Now get up and go home. The moment you set foot in the city, the child will die.
All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He alone of Jeroboam's house will be laid in a grave, because in him was found something good toward the LORD, the God of Israel.

versions.text: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He alone of Jeroboam's house will be laid in a grave, because in him alone the LORD, the God of Israel, found something good.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is passive ("something good was found in him toward the LORD"), not the LORD actively finding; and "alone" is repeated needlessly from the previous clause, where it renders לְבַדּוֹ.

text: Moreover, the LORD will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam—this very day, yes, even now.

And the LORD will strike Israel so that it sways like a reed in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they made their Asherah poles and provoked the LORD to anger.

versions.text: And the LORD will strike Israel until it sways like a reed in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they made their Asherah poles and provoked the LORD to anger.
versions.explanation: כַּאֲשֶׁר means "as/just as," introducing a comparison, not a temporal limit. "Until it sways" misconstrues the image: the striking causes Israel to be shaken like a reed; it does not continue until swaying begins.

text: He will give Israel up because of the sins Jeroboam committed and made Israel commit."
Then Jeroboam's wife got up and went away to Tirzah. As she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.
They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, just as the LORD had said through his servant Ahijah the prophet.
The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.
Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years, and then he lay down with his fathers, and his son Nadab succeeded him as king.

Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel as the place for his name. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
Judah did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. With the sins they committed they provoked him to jealousy more than all their fathers had done.
They too built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were even male cult prostitutes in the land. They committed all the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem.
He carried off the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields Solomon had made.
So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and entrusted them to the commanders of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the royal palace.
Whenever the king went to the house of the LORD, the guards carried the shields, and afterward they returned them to the guardroom.
As for the rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?

versions.text: The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all he did—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
versions.explanation: The em dash breaks the sentence awkwardly for oral reading; a fronted "As for..." clause carries the Hebrew construction more smoothly when read aloud.

text: There was continual war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite, and his son Abijam succeeded him as king.
